title: Creating Searchable Wiki-like Entries in Sites (ChatGPT Only)
author: Aeropar
selftext:
\# Plugins  
Google Drive  
\- Google Sheets

\# Integrations  
Chrome ChatGPT Browser Extension

\# Workflow:   
Disclaimer Requires a lot of Work Usage, preferred Model is 6.1 Sol on Medium, occasionally using Astra (Light/Medium) for heavier tasks that require attention to detail.

\## Steps:   
\- I linked ChatGPT to my Google Drive  
\- I created a Master Tracker for my Project using Google Sheets  
\- I used ChatGPT to create the site using my Legacy Manuscript by exporting my Homebrewery Markdown Source as a .txt file and adding it to my drive, ChatGPT created a folder named “ChatGPT” for which it stored the source and added a tab to list the sources as references in the master tracker. The Site has about a \~256 MB Deployment Limitation.  
\- Integrated Domain Name Mask with NameCheap (  
\- Free Publisher Page on Itch.io holds the downloadable playtest package (about 32MB when counting previous design notes contained within), ChatGPT directs the user here for the download so it doesn’t have to store it within the Website Deployment.  
\- \~500MB Free ImageKit.io Database Integration using Webp files for lossless Compression and SEO optimization (file names / Metadata need adjustments for this benefit)

Result: Deployment Package down to around the same size as the playtest package \~32 MB compared to 254 / 256 MB Limitation. Before Itch/ImageKit integration, with 503 Entries so far all containing Generated Images by ChatGPT that match the game/site’s theme and art style along with filled content regarding Lore, Effects, and other content. 

Takeaway: Offloading Storage through external integrations can reduce the Final Sites Deployment by 87% less of the usage limitation when compared to storing everything within the Site Deployment Package Itself.

Lastly: Feel free to ask me any additional questions below.👇
